## Overview

This report provides a summary analysis of raw TikTok video views stored in `data/raw/video_view.csv`.

```{r}
# Detect correct path relative to working directory
if (basename(getwd()) == "src") {
  data_path <- "../data/raw/video_view.csv"
} else {
  data_path <- "data/raw/video_view.csv"
}

# Load needed packages
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)

# Read dataset
views <- read.csv(data_path)

# Basic exploration
x <- nrow(views)
print(x)

str(views)
head(views)
summary(views)
colSums(is.na(views))

# Summary overview using exact dataset column names
overview <- views %>%
  summarize(
    videos            = n(),
    creators          = n_distinct(creator_id),
    avg_length        = mean(video_length_sec, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_impressions   = mean(impressions_n, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_watched       = mean(watched_n, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_watch_rate    = mean(watch_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_watch_share   = mean(avg_watch_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_watch_seconds = mean(avg_watch_seconds_when_watched, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(overview)

mean(views$watch_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(views$avg_watch_share, na.rm = TRUE)

# Calculate percentage watched
views$watched_pct <- views$watched_n / views$impressions_n * 100

# Identify top video by impressions
topvideo <- views[views$impressions_n == max(views$impressions_n, na.rm = TRUE), ]
print(topvideo)

# Histogram of video lengths
hist(views$video_length_sec)

# Subset high watch rate videos
goodvideos <- subset(views, watch_rate > 0.8)
nrow(goodvideos)
```
